source.text: Ἄγε νῦν οἱ πλούσιοι, κλαύσατε ὀλολύζοντες ἐπὶ ταῖς ταλαιπωρίαις ὑμῶν ταῖς ἐπερχομέναις.

records.literal_gloss: Come now the rich, weep wailing over the miseries of you the [ones] coming.

en.L: Come now, you rich, weep, wailing over your miseries that are coming.
en.B: Listen now, you who are rich: weep and cry out in grief over the miseries that are about to fall on you.
en.R: You who are rich, listen to this! Cry and howl, because terrible troubles are on their way to you.

es.L: ¡Ea, ahora, ricos! {{plural_you:Lloren|Llorad}} dando alaridos por {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} miserias que se acercan.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} ahora, ricos: {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} y {{plural_you:giman|gemid}} de dolor por las desgracias que están a punto de caer sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los ricos, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} esto: {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} a gritos, porque {{plural_you:les|os}} vienen encima sufrimientos terribles.

sw.L: Haya sasa, enyi matajiri, lieni mkipiga yowe kwa ajili ya taabu zenu zinazowajia.
sw.B: Sikilizeni sasa, enyi matajiri: lieni na kuomboleza kwa sauti kuu kwa sababu ya mateso yanayokaribia kuwapata.
sw.R: Ninyi matajiri, sikilizeni! Lieni na kupiga kelele za huzuni, kwa sababu taabu kubwa zinakuja juu yenu.

decisions.choice: come now: a call to attention, as in 4:13
decisions.reason: Ἄγε is a fixed imperative, "come!", used to get someone's attention, and νῦν adds "now". James opened 4:13 with the same words to address traders who make plans without God; here he turns to the rich.

decisions.choice: the rich: wealthy people outside the community who oppress it
decisions.reason: James does not call them brothers and sisters and does not call them to repent. He describes them cheating their workers and condemning the righteous (verses 4-6), as the rich of 2:6-7 drag believers into court and slander the name they bear. The words are spoken to them in the manner of the prophets' oracles against the nations, which God's people overhear; verse 7 turns back to the brothers and sisters.

decisions.choice: weep and wail: the cry of those facing the day of the Lord
decisions.reason: ὀλολύζω is a loud, howling lament. The prophets call for the same cry from those about to be judged: "Howl, for the day of the LORD is close" (Isaiah 13:6; see Isaiah 15:2-3; Amos 8:3). The miseries "that are coming" are that judgment, which verses 7-9 connect with the coming of the Lord.

decisions.choice: Listen now; You who are rich, listen to this! ... terrible troubles
decisions.reason: "Come now" is a call to attention, not an invitation to come (m1). Balanced says "Listen now", as at 4:13. Readable puts the call to attention (m1) into plain words and says "terrible troubles" for the miseries.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: As throughout the letter, each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). Verses 1-6 speak to the rich rather than to the believers, but they are still a plural "you", so they carry the same setting.

decisions.choice: ¡Ea, ahora
decisions.reason: "Vengan" would sound like an invitation to come. "¡Ea!" is the Spanish interjection that rouses a listener, as the Greek fixed imperative does (m1); Balanced and Readable say "escuchen".

source.text: ὁ πλοῦτος ὑμῶν σέσηπεν, καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια ὑμῶν σητόβρωτα γέγονεν, ὁ χρυσὸς ὑμῶν καὶ ὁ ἄργυρος κατίωται, καὶ ὁ ἰὸς αὐτῶν εἰς μαρτύριον ὑμῖν ἔσται καὶ φάγεται τὰς σάρκας ὑμῶν· ὡς πῦρ ἐθησαυρίσατε ἐν ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις.

records.literal_gloss: The wealth of you has rotted, and the garments of you moth-eaten have become, \v 3 the gold of you and the silver has corroded, and the corrosion of them for a testimony to you will be and will eat the flesh of you; like fire you stored up in [the] last days.

en.L: Your wealth has rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten; \v 3 your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be a witness against you and will eat your flesh. Like fire [is what] you stored up in [the] last days.
en.B: Your riches have rotted away, and your clothes have been eaten by moths. \v 3 Your gold and silver have corroded, and the corrosion on them will stand as evidence against you and will devour your flesh. What you have heaped up in the last days is like fire.
en.R: Your riches are rotting. Moths have eaten your fine clothes. \v 3 Your gold and silver are covered with rust. That rust will be proof against you, and it will eat your bodies. You have piled up riches in the last days, and they are like a fire.

es.L: {{plural_you:Su|Vuestra}} riqueza se ha podrido, y {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} ropas están comidas de polilla; \v 3 {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} oro y {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} plata se han corroído, y la corrosión de ellos será un testimonio contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y comerá {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} carnes. Como fuego [es lo que] {{plural_you:atesoraron|atesorasteis}} en [los] últimos días.
es.B: {{plural_you:Sus|Vuestras}} riquezas se han podrido, y la polilla se ha comido {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} ropa. \v 3 {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} oro y {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} plata se han corroído, y esa corrosión servirá de prueba contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y devorará {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} carne. Lo que {{plural_you:han amontonado|habéis amontonado}} en los últimos días es como fuego.
es.R: {{plural_you:Sus|Vuestras}} riquezas se están pudriendo. La polilla se ha comido {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} ropa fina. \v 3 {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} oro y {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} plata están cubiertos de óxido. Ese óxido será una prueba contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:les|os}} comerá el cuerpo. {{plural_you:Han acumulado|Habéis acumulado}} riquezas en los últimos días, y son como un fuego.

sw.L: Utajiri wenu umeoza, na mavazi yenu yameliwa na nondo; \v 3 dhahabu yenu na fedha zimeingia kutu, na kutu yake itakuwa ushahidi dhidi yenu, nayo itakula miili yenu. [Ni] kama moto mlichojilimbikizia katika siku za mwisho.
sw.B: Mali zenu zimeoza, na nguo zenu zimeliwa na nondo. \v 3 Dhahabu yenu na fedha yenu zimeingia kutu, na kutu hiyo itakuwa ushahidi dhidi yenu na itakula miili yenu. Mlichojilimbikizia katika siku za mwisho ni kama moto.
sw.R: Mali zenu zinaoza. Nondo wamekula nguo zenu nzuri. \v 3 Dhahabu yenu na fedha yenu zimefunikwa na kutu. Kutu hiyo itakuwa ushahidi dhidi yenu, nayo itakula miili yenu. Mmejilimbikizia mali katika siku za mwisho, nazo ni kama moto.

decisions.choice: have rotted, have become moth-eaten, have corroded: the coming judgment told as already done
alternatives: a plain description of wealth spoiling as it is hoarded
decisions.reason: The verbs σέσηπεν, γέγονεν and κατίωται are perfects, describing a finished state. The prophets speak of God's coming judgment as if it had already happened, and James does the same. The picture is also true to life: grain, fine clothing and coins hoarded and never used spoil. Jesus warned against treasure on earth "where moth and rust destroy" (Matthew 6:19-20).

decisions.choice: corrosion: the dull coat that gathers on gold and silver
decisions.reason: Gold does not rust and silver only tarnishes, so ἰός here is the coating that unused metal gathers, the sign of wealth stored away and never put to use. The same word means venom in 3:8, which suits its being said to eat flesh.

decisions.choice: a witness against you
decisions.reason: εἰς μαρτύριον ὑμῖν is literally "for a testimony to you". In a scene of judgment the testimony is against them, as in Mark 6:11, where the same phrase means a witness against those who refused the disciples.

decisions.choice: like fire you stored up: "like fire" goes with what they stored up, as the SBLGNT punctuates
alternatives: will eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in the last days
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a raised dot before ὡς πῦρ, so "like fire" belongs with ἐθησαυρίσατε, "you stored up": what they heaped up is like fire laid up against themselves (compare "storing up wrath", Romans 2:5). Other editions punctuate after "fire", so that the corrosion eats their flesh like fire, and the next clause is simply "you stored up treasure in the last days". Either way the picture is judgment. They hoarded in the last days, when the Lord's coming is near (5:8), the very time when wealth should have been shared.

decisions.choice: stored up treasure / heaped up
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to store up treasure and needs no object; Literal and Balanced say what was stored without adding a word for it.

decisions.choice: rust
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for the coating on the metal (m2).

decisions.choice: atesoraron (Literal); han amontonado (Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Atesorar" is to lay up treasure, the sense of the Greek verb, and it is the word used for storing up wrath in Romans 2:5, which the meaning decision compares (m4). Balanced says "amontonar", heaping up, which keeps the picture without needing an object.

decisions.choice: zimeingia kutu; kutu
decisions.reason: Swahili "kutu" is the coat that forms on any metal, so it serves at every level for the dull coating of the meaning decision (m2) without claiming that gold rusts.

decisions.choice: mlichojilimbikizia
decisions.reason: "Kujilimbikizia" (to pile up for oneself) is the verb Romans 2:5 uses for storing up wrath, which the meaning decision compares (m4).

source.text: ἰδοὺ ὁ μισθὸς τῶν ἐργατῶν τῶν ἀμησάντων τὰς χώρας ὑμῶν ὁ ἀφυστερημένος ἀφ’ ὑμῶν κράζει, καὶ αἱ βοαὶ τῶν θερισάντων εἰς τὰ ὦτα Κυρίου Σαβαὼθ εἰσεληλύθασιν·

records.literal_gloss: Look the wage of the workers of the [ones] having mowed the fields of you, the [wage] having been held back by you, cries out, and the cries of the [ones] having harvested into the ears of [the] Lord of Sabaoth have entered;

en.L: Look, the wage of the workers who mowed your fields, which has been held back by you, cries out, and the cries of those who harvested have entered into the ears of [the] Lord of Sabaoth.
en.B: Listen! The pay you held back from the laborers who mowed your fields is crying out, and the shouts of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Armies.
en.R: Look! You did not pay the workers who cut the grain in your fields. Their unpaid wages are crying out, and the cries of those workers have reached the ears of the Lord of Armies.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, el salario de los obreros que segaron {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} campos, retenido por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, clama, y los clamores de los que cosecharon han entrado en los oídos del Señor de los ejércitos.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! El jornal que {{plural_you:retuvieron|retuvisteis}} a los trabajadores que segaron {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} campos está clamando, y los gritos de los segadores han llegado a los oídos del Señor de los ejércitos.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! {{plural_you:Ustedes no les pagaron|Vosotros no les pagasteis}} a los trabajadores que cosecharon el grano en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} campos. Ese salario que no recibieron está clamando, y los gritos de esos trabajadores han llegado a los oídos del Señor de los ejércitos.

sw.L: Tazameni, ujira wa wafanyakazi waliovuna mashamba yenu, uliozuiliwa nanyi, unalia, na vilio vya wavunaji vimeingia masikioni mwa Bwana wa majeshi.
sw.B: Sikilizeni! Ujira wa vibarua waliovuna mashamba yenu, ambao mliuzuia, unalia, na vilio vya wavunaji vimefika masikioni mwa Bwana wa majeshi.
sw.R: Tazameni! Hamkuwalipa wafanyakazi waliovuna mashamba yenu. Ujira wao ambao hawakulipwa unalia, na vilio vya wafanyakazi hao vimefika masikioni mwa Bwana wa majeshi.

decisions.choice: wages held back cry out: the Law's command to pay a worker the same day
decisions.reason: Day laborers were hired by the day and paid at evening (Matthew 20:8), and they lived on that pay. The Law commands that a hired worker be paid before the sun goes down, so that he does not cry out to the LORD against his employer (Deuteronomy 24:14-15; see Leviticus 19:13; Malachi 3:5). Like Abel's blood (Genesis 4:10), the wrong itself cries out to God.

decisions.choice: ἀφυστερημένος: held back (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, including the later Byzantine tradition, read a form of ἀποστερέω, "rob, defraud", in place of ἀφυστερέω, "hold back, withhold", which the SBLGNT reads with early manuscripts such as Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. The sense is close: the workers were not paid. This is described from general knowledge and must be checked against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Lord of Sabaoth: the Hebrew title Yahweh of hosts
decisions.reason: Σαβαὼθ is the Hebrew word for "armies" or "hosts" written in Greek letters, as the Greek Old Testament often keeps it (Romans 9:29, quoting Isaiah 1:9). The title presents God as commander of all the powers of heaven and earth. Isaiah 5:9 uses it of the Lord who has heard the injustice of those who add field to field. The powerless workers have the most powerful hearer.

decisions.choice: Lord of Sabaoth (Literal); Lord of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew title in the form the Greek keeps it. Balanced and Readable translate what it means (m3), since "hosts" is no longer a clear English word.

decisions.choice: You did not pay the workers ... Their unpaid wages are crying out
decisions.reason: Readable states the wrong first in a short sentence and then gives the picture of the wages crying out.

decisions.choice: Señor de los ejércitos
decisions.reason: Unlike English "hosts", the Spanish title "Señor de los ejércitos" is long established and still clear, so every level translates what the Hebrew word means (m3) instead of keeping it as Literal English does.

decisions.choice: Bwana wa majeshi
decisions.reason: "Bwana wa majeshi" is the established Swahili form of the title and says what the Hebrew word means (m3), so every level uses it instead of keeping the Hebrew word as Literal English does.

source.text: ἐτρυφήσατε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐσπαταλήσατε, ἐθρέψατε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ σφαγῆς.

records.literal_gloss: You lived in luxury upon the earth and lived for pleasure, you fattened the hearts of you in [a] day of slaughter.

en.L: You lived softly on the earth and indulged yourselves; you fed your hearts fat in a day of slaughter.
en.B: Your life on earth has been soft and given over to pleasure. You have fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter.
en.R: You have lived an easy life here on earth, doing whatever you enjoyed. You have stuffed yourselves like animals that are being fattened to be killed.

es.L: {{plural_you:Vivieron|Vivisteis}} en el lujo sobre la tierra y {{plural_you:se dieron|os disteis}} a los placeres; {{plural_you:engordaron|engordasteis}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones en un día de matanza.
es.B: {{plural_you:Han llevado|Habéis llevado}} en la tierra una vida de lujo y de placeres. {{plural_you:Han engordado|Habéis engordado}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón en un día de matanza.
es.R: {{plural_you:Han vivido|Habéis vivido}} aquí en la tierra con toda comodidad, haciendo todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} daba placer. {{plural_you:Se han atiborrado|Os habéis atiborrado}} como animales que se engordan para matarlos.

sw.L: Mliishi kwa anasa juu ya dunia, mkajitosa katika starehe; mlinenepesha mioyo yenu katika siku ya machinjo.
sw.B: Maisha yenu duniani yamekuwa ya anasa na ya kujifurahisha. Mmenenepesha mioyo yenu katika siku ya machinjo.
sw.R: Mmeishi maisha ya raha hapa duniani, mkifanya kila kitu mlichopenda. Mmejishibisha kama wanyama wanaonenepeshwa ili wachinjwe.

decisions.choice: lived in luxury and self-indulgence
decisions.reason: τρυφάω is soft, pampered living; σπαταλάω is living for pleasure without restraint (1 Timothy 5:6 uses it of a widow who lives for pleasure). "On the earth" sets their comfort here against the Lord who hears from heaven (verse 4) and the judgment to come.

decisions.choice: fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter: like animals fattened for slaughter, they have fed themselves while their judgment is at hand
alternatives: they feasted on a day of slaughter, as at a festival meal
they fed themselves while the poor were being killed (verse 6)
decisions.reason: The heart is the whole inner self. Jeremiah asks God to set the wicked apart "like sheep for the slaughter... for the day of slaughter" (Jeremiah 12:3; see Jeremiah 25:34; Isaiah 34:2, 6). The rich have been feeding themselves up, unaware that the day of slaughter is theirs.

decisions.choice: lived softly; indulged yourselves
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two verbs as two short statements without smoothing them into one phrase.

decisions.choice: like animals that are being fattened to be killed
alternatives: You have fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter.
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture (m2) that Literal and Balanced leave as "fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter".

source.text: κατεδικάσατε, ἐφονεύσατε τὸν δίκαιον.

records.literal_gloss: You condemned, you murdered the righteous [one].

en.L: You condemned, you murdered the righteous one.
en.B: You have condemned and murdered the righteous.
en.R: You have condemned people who did what was right, and you have killed them.

es.L: {{plural_you:Condenaron|Condenasteis}}, {{plural_you:asesinaron|asesinasteis}} al justo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Han condenado|Habéis condenado}} y {{plural_you:han asesinado|habéis asesinado}} al justo.
es.R: {{plural_you:Han condenado|Habéis condenado}} a personas que hacían lo correcto, y las {{plural_you:han|habéis}} matado.

sw.L: Mlimhukumu, mlimuua mwenye haki.
sw.B: Mmemhukumu na kumuua mwenye haki.
sw.R: Mmewahukumu watu wanaotenda haki, na mmewaua.

decisions.choice: the righteous one: any righteous person the rich oppress
decisions.reason: The singular with the article stands for a whole class, as in Psalm 37:12, 32, where the wicked lie in wait to kill the righteous, and Amos 2:6; 5:12. In context these are the poor workers of verse 4. Readers have also heard Jesus here, whom Acts calls "the Righteous One" whom his hearers murdered (Acts 3:14; 7:52), but nothing in the passage points to a single event.

decisions.choice: condemned, murdered: through the courts and by taking away the means of life
decisions.reason: The two verbs stand side by side without "and", like two blows. The rich drag the poor into court (2:6), and condemnation led to death, whether by sentence or by stripping the poor of the wages they needed to live (verse 4).

decisions.choice: the righteous
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the English collective "the righteous" for the Greek singular that stands for a class (m1).

decisions.choice: people who did what was right
decisions.reason: Readable says in plain words who "the righteous" are and makes the class plural (m1).

source.text: οὐκ ἀντιτάσσεται ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Not does he resist you?

en.L: Does he not resist you?
en.B: Does he not oppose you?
en.R: Is he not standing against you?

es.L: ¿No se {{plural_you:les|os}} opone?
es.B: ¿Acaso no se {{plural_you:les|os}} opone?
es.R: ¿No se levanta él contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?

sw.L: Je, hawapingi ninyi?
sw.B: Je, yeye hawapingi ninyi?
sw.R: Je, yeye hasimami dhidi yenu?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer yes, as the SBLGNT punctuates
alternatives: a statement: he does not resist you
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the sentence with a question mark, and οὐκ in a question expects the answer "yes": does he not oppose you? Other editions print a statement, "he does not resist you": the righteous suffer without fighting back (Isaiah 53:7). The text is followed here.

decisions.choice: he: the one murdered, now standing against them, or God
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It may be the righteous one, who though dead stands against them before God, as Abel's blood cried out (Genesis 4:10). It may be God: James used the same verb in 4:6, "God opposes the proud". Both point to the judgment that verses 7-9 announce.

decisions.choice: he, with no capital-letter setting
decisions.reason: Because the subject may be the righteous one or God (m2), every level keeps a plain "he" and does not mark it as a pronoun for God.

source.text: Μακροθυμήσατε οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ἕως τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ κυρίου.

records.literal_gloss: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord.

en.L: Be patient therefore, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, until the coming of the Lord.
en.B: So then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, wait patiently until the Lord comes.
en.R: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, be patient until the Lord comes back.

es.L: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} paciencia, pues, hermanos, hasta la venida del Señor.
es.B: Así que, hermanos, {{plural_you:esperen|esperad}} con paciencia hasta que el Señor venga.
es.R: Por eso, hermanos, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} paciencia hasta que el Señor vuelva.

sw.L: Kuweni na subira basi, ndugu, mpaka kuja kwa Bwana.
sw.B: Basi, ndugu, ngojeni kwa subira mpaka Bwana atakapokuja.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, ndugu, kuweni na subira mpaka Bwana atakaporudi.

decisions.choice: so then: because the Lord will judge the oppressors
decisions.reason: οὖν draws the conclusion from verses 1-6. Because the Lord will deal with those who wrong them, the believers, now addressed again as brothers and sisters, can wait without taking matters into their own hands.

decisions.choice: be patient: hold out under delay and provocation
decisions.reason: μακροθυμέω is patience over a long time, being slow to give up or to strike back. It is different from ὑπομένω, endurance under trial (verse 11; 1:3-4, 12); this translation says "patient" for the one and "endure" for the other.

decisions.choice: the coming of the Lord: the arrival of the Lord Jesus at the end
decisions.reason: παρουσία was used of a ruler's arrival on an official visit, and it is the regular word for Jesus' coming at the end (Matthew 24:3, 27; 1 Thessalonians 4:15; 2 Peter 3:4). In James "Lord" names both God and Jesus (1:1; 2:1); with "coming" it is Jesus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James is writing to the whole community of believers (1:1), women as well as men (2:15 speaks of a brother or sister), so the inclusive default says so. Traditional is one tap away.

decisions.choice: until the Lord comes / comes back
alternatives: until the coming of the Lord
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the noun "coming" into a verb. Readable says "comes back" because this is the return of Jesus (m3).

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in this translation, Spanish "hermanos" already includes sisters, so it carries no gender setting.

decisions.choice: paciencia (be patient)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision keeps patience apart from endurance (m2). Spanish says "paciencia" for this verb and its noun in verses 7-10, and "perseverar" / "perseverancia" for endurance in verse 11.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" means brother or sister, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Swahili in this chapter.

decisions.choice: subira (be patient)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision keeps patience apart from endurance (m2). Swahili says "kuwa na subira" for this verb and its noun in verses 7-10, as Romans 2:4 uses "subira" for patience, and "kustahimili" / "ustahimilivu" for endurance in verse 11.

source.text: ἰδοὺ ὁ γεωργὸς ἐκδέχεται τὸν τίμιον καρπὸν τῆς γῆς, μακροθυμῶν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἕως λάβῃ πρόϊμον καὶ ὄψιμον.

records.literal_gloss: Look the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it until it receives early and late.

en.L: Look, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it until it receives [the] early and late [rains].
en.B: Think of the farmer, who waits for the land to yield its precious harvest and is patient over it until the early and late rains have come.
en.R: Think about farmers. They wait for their land to give its valuable crop. They are patient until the rain comes in the fall and again in the spring.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, el labrador aguarda el precioso fruto de la tierra, teniendo paciencia con él hasta que reciba la [lluvia] temprana y la tardía.
es.B: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en el agricultor: espera a que la tierra le dé su valiosa cosecha y aguarda con paciencia hasta que hayan llegado las lluvias tempranas y las tardías.
es.R: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en los agricultores. Esperan que su tierra dé una buena cosecha. Tienen paciencia hasta que llegan las lluvias de la siembra y, después, las que caen antes de la cosecha.

sw.L: Tazameni, mkulima anangoja matunda ya thamani ya ardhi, akiwa na subira juu yake mpaka yapate [mvua] za mwanzo na za mwisho.
sw.B: Mfikirieni mkulima: anangoja ardhi itoe mazao yake ya thamani, naye huyangoja kwa subira mpaka mvua za mwanzo na za mwisho zinyeshe.
sw.R: Fikirieni wakulima. Wanangoja ardhi yao itoe mazao mazuri. Wanangoja kwa subira mpaka mvua za wakati wa kupanda zinyeshe, na baadaye mvua za kabla ya mavuno.

decisions.choice: early and late rains: the autumn rains at sowing and the spring rains before harvest
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel the first rains come in autumn and soften the ground for sowing; the last come in spring and fill out the grain. Without both there is no harvest, and the farmer cannot hurry them. The phrase comes from the Old Testament (Deuteronomy 11:14; Jeremiah 5:24; Joel 2:23), where the rains are God's gift.

decisions.choice: "the early and the late" with no noun (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has the two adjectives alone. Some manuscripts add ὑετὸν, "rain", and some add "fruit". The sense is rain either way, as the Old Testament phrase shows. This is described from general knowledge and must be checked against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: being patient over it until it receives: the farmer waits for the crop until it has had the rains
decisions.reason: αὐτῷ "it" is the fruit; the subject of λάβῃ, "receives", is most naturally the same crop. The farmer is the model of the patience James has just called for ("be patient", μακροθυμῶν, the same verb).

decisions.choice: rains
decisions.reason: The Greek gives only the adjectives "early" and "late"; English needs the noun (m2). Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: the rain in the fall and again in the spring
decisions.reason: Readable explains when the early and late rains come (m1).

decisions.choice: las lluvias de la siembra y las que caen antes de la cosecha
alternatives: la lluvia de otoño y la de primavera
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two rains (m1) by what they do rather than by season, because many Spanish readers live where autumn and spring fall in other months.

decisions.choice: mvua za wakati wa kupanda ... mvua za kabla ya mavuno
alternatives: mvua za vuli na za masika
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two rains (m1) by what they do. East Africa's own short and long rains ("vuli", "masika") fall in different months from Israel's, so naming them would mislead.

source.text: μακροθυμήσατε καὶ ὑμεῖς, στηρίξατε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἡ παρουσία τοῦ κυρίου ἤγγικεν.

records.literal_gloss: Be patient also you, strengthen the hearts of you, because the coming of the Lord has drawn near.

en.L: You also be patient; make your hearts firm, because the coming of the Lord has drawn near.
en.B: You must be patient as well. Make your hearts firm, for the Lord's coming has drawn near.
en.R: You also must be patient. Make your hearts strong, because the Lord will soon be here.

es.L: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} paciencia también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; {{plural_you:afirmen|afirmad}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones, porque la venida del Señor se ha acercado.
es.B: También {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} tener paciencia. {{plural_you:Afirmen|Afirmad}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón, porque la venida del Señor se ha acercado.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} también {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} que ser pacientes. {{plural_you:Fortalezcan|Fortaleced}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón, porque el Señor llegará pronto.

sw.L: Kuweni na subira nanyi pia; imarisheni mioyo yenu, kwa sababu kuja kwa Bwana kumekaribia.
sw.B: Ninyi pia mnapaswa kuwa na subira. Imarisheni mioyo yenu, kwa maana kuja kwa Bwana kumekaribia.
sw.R: Ninyi pia kuweni na subira. Tieni mioyo yenu nguvu, kwa sababu Bwana atakuja hivi karibuni.

decisions.choice: you also: like the farmer
decisions.reason: καὶ ὑμεῖς, "you too", applies the farmer's example directly to the readers.

decisions.choice: strengthen your hearts: make your resolve firm so that it does not waver
decisions.reason: στηρίζω means to make firm or establish; Paul prays that God will "establish your hearts" until the Lord Jesus comes (1 Thessalonians 3:13). The heart is the center of will and purpose. This is the opposite of the double-minded person (1:8; 4:8).

decisions.choice: has drawn near: the Lord's coming is close
decisions.reason: ἤγγικεν is a perfect, "has come near", the word used of the kingdom (Mark 1:15) and of the end (Romans 13:12; 1 Peter 4:7). James gives no date; he says the coming is near enough to shape how they live now.

decisions.choice: will soon be here
decisions.reason: Readable expresses nearness in time in everyday words (m3).

source.text: μὴ στενάζετε, ἀδελφοί, κατ’ ἀλλήλων, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε· ἰδοὺ ὁ κριτὴς πρὸ τῶν θυρῶν ἕστηκεν.

records.literal_gloss: Not groan, brothers, against one another, so that not you be judged; look, the judge before the doors stands.

en.L: Do not groan against one another, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, so that you are not judged; look, the Judge stands in front of the doors.
en.B: Stop complaining about one another, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, or you yourselves will be judged. Look: the Judge is already standing at the doors.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, do not complain about each other, or you will be judged. Look! The Judge is standing right outside the door.

es.L: No {{plural_you:giman|gimáis}} unos contra otros, hermanos, para que no {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} juzgados; {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, el Juez está de pie delante de las puertas.
es.B: {{plural_you:Dejen de quejarse|Dejad de quejaros}} unos de otros, hermanos, o {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} juzgados. {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}: el Juez ya está de pie a las puertas.
es.R: Hermanos, no {{plural_you:se quejen|os quejéis}} unos de otros, o {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} juzgados. ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! El Juez está justo al otro lado de la puerta.

sw.L: Msinung'unikiane, ndugu, ili msihukumiwe; tazameni, Hakimu amesimama mbele ya milango.
sw.B: Acheni kulalamikiana, ndugu, la sivyo ninyi wenyewe mtahukumiwa. Tazameni, Hakimu amekwisha kusimama mlangoni.
sw.R: Ndugu, msilalamikiane, la sivyo mtahukumiwa. Tazameni! Hakimu amesimama nje ya mlango, tayari kuingia.

decisions.choice: groan against one another: complain and lay blame on each other
decisions.reason: στενάζω is to sigh or groan. Directed "against one another" it is the muttered complaint of people under pressure who turn on each other instead of waiting for the Lord.

decisions.choice: so that you are not judged
decisions.reason: This echoes Jesus' words, "Judge not, that you be not judged" (Matthew 7:1), and James's own warning that speaking against a brother or sister is judging them (4:11-12).

decisions.choice: the Judge stands at the doors: he is about to come in
decisions.reason: To be "at the doors" is to be on the point of arriving (Mark 13:29; compare Revelation 3:20). The Judge is the Lord whose coming is near (verse 8), the one lawgiver and judge of 4:12.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James is writing to the whole community of believers (1:1), women as well as men (2:15 speaks of a brother or sister), so the inclusive default says so. Traditional is one tap away.

decisions.choice: complain about
decisions.reason: "Groan" is kept at Literal to show the word; Balanced and Readable say what the groaning is (m1).

decisions.choice: msinung'unikiane
decisions.reason: "Kuugua" is to groan with pain or illness and could suggest being sick. Literal says "kunung'unikiana", to grumble against one another, which keeps the sound of the word and says what the groaning is (m1).

source.text: ὑπόδειγμα λάβετε, ἀδελφοί, τῆς κακοπαθίας καὶ τῆς μακροθυμίας τοὺς προφήτας, οἳ ἐλάλησαν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου.

records.literal_gloss: [As] an example take, brothers, of the suffering and of the patience the prophets, who spoke in the name of [the] Lord.

en.L: Take, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, as an example of suffering hardship and of patience the prophets, who spoke in the name of [the] Lord.
en.B: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, look to the prophets who spoke in the Lord's name, and take them as your example of hardship borne with patience.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, think about the prophets who spoke for the Lord. They suffered hard things, and they were patient. Follow their example.

es.L: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}}, hermanos, como ejemplo del sufrimiento y de la paciencia a los profetas, que hablaron en el nombre del Señor.
es.B: Hermanos, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} a los profetas que hablaron en nombre del Señor, y {{plural_you:tómenlos|tomadlos}} como ejemplo de sufrimiento soportado con paciencia.
es.R: Hermanos, {{plural_you:piensen|pensad}} en los profetas que hablaron de parte del Señor. Ellos sufrieron cosas muy duras y fueron pacientes. {{plural_you:Sigan|Seguid}} su ejemplo.

sw.L: Chukueni manabii, ndugu, kuwa mfano wa mateso na wa subira, wale waliosema kwa jina la Bwana.
sw.B: Ndugu, watazameni manabii waliosema kwa jina la Bwana, na kuwafanya kuwa mfano wenu: walipatwa na mateso, wakawa na subira.
sw.R: Ndugu, wafikirieni manabii waliosema kwa niaba ya Bwana. Walipata mateso makali, lakini walikuwa na subira. Fuateni mfano wao.

decisions.choice: suffering and patience: hardship borne with patience
decisions.reason: κακοπαθία is enduring hardship or ill treatment (the verb comes in verse 13), and μακροθυμία is the patience of verses 7-8. Joined by "and", the two describe one example: the prophets suffered and waited patiently through it.

decisions.choice: the prophets: messengers of God who suffered for their message
decisions.reason: Jeremiah was beaten and put in the stocks (Jeremiah 20:2); Elijah was hunted for his life (1 Kings 19:10); Jesus spoke of the prophets persecuted before his followers (Matthew 5:12; 23:37).

decisions.choice: spoke in the name of the Lord: as God's messengers, with his authority
decisions.reason: To speak in someone's name is to speak as their representative. The prophets said "Thus says the LORD"; their faithfulness to the message brought their suffering. "Lord" here is God.

decisions.choice: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}
decisions.reason: James is writing to the whole community of believers (1:1), women as well as men (2:15 speaks of a brother or sister), so the inclusive default says so. Traditional is one tap away.

decisions.choice: the prophets first, then the example
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the prophets before saying what they are an example of, which reads more easily than the Greek order.

source.text: ἰδοὺ μακαρίζομεν τοὺς ὑπομείναντας· τὴν ὑπομονὴν Ἰὼβ ἠκούσατε, καὶ τὸ τέλος κυρίου εἴδετε, ὅτι πολύσπλαγχνός ἐστιν ὁ κύριος καὶ οἰκτίρμων.

records.literal_gloss: Look we call blessed those having endured; the endurance of Job you heard, and the end of [the] Lord you saw, that very compassionate is the Lord and merciful.

en.L: Look, we call blessed those who endured. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and you have seen the outcome [from the] Lord, that the Lord is full of compassion and merciful.
en.B: Indeed, we call those who endured blessed. You have heard of Job's endurance, and you have seen the outcome the Lord gave, for the Lord is rich in compassion and mercy.
en.R: We say that people who endured are blessed. You have heard how Job endured. And you have seen how the Lord was good to him in the end. The Lord cares deeply and is full of mercy.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, llamamos bienaventurados a los que perseveraron. {{plural_you:Oyeron|Oísteis}} de la perseverancia de Job, y {{plural_you:vieron|visteis}} el desenlace [que dio el] Señor, que el Señor es muy compasivo y misericordioso.
es.B: En verdad, llamamos bienaventurados a los que perseveraron. {{plural_you:Han oído|Habéis oído}} de la perseverancia de Job, y {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}} el desenlace que le dio el Señor, porque el Señor es rico en compasión y misericordia.
es.R: Decimos que Dios bendice a los que perseveraron. {{plural_you:Ustedes han oído|Vosotros habéis oído}} cómo Job perseveró. Y {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}} cómo al final el Señor fue bueno con él. El Señor tiene un corazón muy compasivo y está lleno de misericordia.

sw.L: Tazameni, tunawaita heri wale waliostahimili; mmesikia habari ya ustahimilivu wa Ayubu, na mmeuona mwisho [aliotoa] Bwana, kwamba Bwana ni mwingi wa huruma na mwenye rehema.
sw.B: Kwa kweli tunawaita heri wale waliostahimili. Mmesikia habari za ustahimilivu wa Ayubu, na mmeuona mwisho ambao Bwana alimpa, kwa maana Bwana ni mwingi wa huruma na rehema.
sw.R: Tunasema kwamba watu waliostahimili wamebarikiwa. Mmesikia jinsi Ayubu alivyostahimili. Tena mmeona jinsi Bwana alivyomtendea mema mwishoni. Bwana anajali sana, naye amejaa rehema.

decisions.choice: we call blessed those who endured
decisions.reason: James repeats his opening beatitude, "Blessed is the man who endures trial" (1:12), and Jesus' blessing on the persecuted (Matthew 5:10-12).

decisions.choice: endurance: holding on under pressure
decisions.reason: ὑπομένω and ὑπομονή are not passive waiting but holding fast under trial (1:3-4, 12). Job protests and questions, but he does not let go of God (Job 1:21-22; 2:10).

decisions.choice: the outcome from the Lord: what the Lord finally brought about for Job
decisions.reason: τέλος is an end, outcome or goal. Job's story ends with the Lord restoring him (Job 42:10-17), and the clause that follows says what they saw in it: the Lord is compassionate and merciful. It can also be read as the Lord's purpose in Job's trials; the two come to the same thing.

decisions.choice: full of compassion and merciful: the Lord's own self-description
decisions.reason: πολύσπλαγχνος is built from "much" and the inner parts, the seat of feeling: deeply compassionate. With οἰκτίρμων it recalls the Lord's words to Moses, "merciful and gracious" (Exodus 34:6), repeated in Psalm 103:8 and 111:4.

decisions.choice: how the Lord was good to him in the end
decisions.reason: Readable says what the outcome was (m3), naming the Lord's kindness to Job.

decisions.choice: bienaventurados (L, B); Dios bendice a (R)
decisions.reason: The same word as the beatitude in James 1:12 ("Bienaventurado") and Romans 14:22, so the reader hears that James is picking up his own earlier blessing. "Dichosos" is more current, and a reviewer may prefer it in all three places. Readable says "Dios bendice a", as James 1:12 Readable does.

decisions.choice: wamebarikiwa
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the beatitude word "heri" (m1). Readable says "wamebarikiwa", they are blessed, which a young reader understands at once.

source.text: Πρὸ πάντων δέ, ἀδελφοί μου, μὴ ὀμνύετε, μήτε τὸν οὐρανὸν μήτε τὴν γῆν μήτε ἄλλον τινὰ ὅρκον· ἤτω δὲ ὑμῶν τὸ Ναὶ ναὶ καὶ τὸ Οὒ οὔ, ἵνα μὴ ὑπὸ κρίσιν πέσητε.

records.literal_gloss: Before all but, brothers of me, not swear, neither the heaven nor the earth nor other any oath; let be but of you the Yes yes and the No no, so that not under judgment you fall.

en.L: But above all, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, do not swear, neither [by] heaven nor [by] the earth nor [by] any other oath; but let your Yes be yes, and [your] No no, so that you do not fall under judgment.
en.B: Above everything else, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, do not swear oaths, whether by heaven or by earth or by anything else. When you say yes, let it be a plain yes, and when you say no, a plain no, so that you do not fall under judgment.
en.R: Most important of all, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, do not make a promise by swearing an oath. Do not swear by heaven or by the earth or by anything else. Just say "Yes" or "No" and mean it. Then you will not be judged.

es.L: Pero sobre todo, hermanos míos, no {{plural_you:juren|juréis}}, ni [por] el cielo ni [por] la tierra ni [por] ningún otro juramento; sino que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Sí sea sí, y el No, no, para que no {{plural_you:caigan|caigáis}} bajo juicio.
es.B: Por encima de todo, hermanos míos, no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} juramentos, ni por el cielo ni por la tierra ni por ninguna otra cosa. Cuando {{plural_you:digan|digáis}} sí, que sea un sí sin más, y cuando {{plural_you:digan|digáis}} no, un no sin más, para que no {{plural_you:caigan|caigáis}} bajo juicio.
es.R: Lo más importante de todo, hermanos míos: no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} promesas jurando. No {{plural_you:juren|juréis}} por el cielo ni por la tierra ni por ninguna otra cosa. Solo {{plural_you:digan|decid}} «sí» o «no», y que sea verdad. Así no {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} juzgados.

sw.L: Lakini zaidi ya yote, ndugu zangu, msiape, wala [kwa] mbingu wala [kwa] dunia wala kiapo kingine chochote; bali Ndiyo yenu iwe ndiyo, na Hapana [yenu] iwe hapana, ili msianguke chini ya hukumu.
sw.B: Zaidi ya yote, ndugu zangu, msiape viapo, iwe kwa mbingu au kwa dunia au kwa kitu kingine chochote. Mkisema ndiyo, iwe ndiyo tu, na mkisema hapana, iwe hapana tu, ili msianguke chini ya hukumu.
sw.R: Jambo kubwa kuliko yote, ndugu zangu, msitoe ahadi kwa kuapa. Msiape kwa mbingu wala kwa dunia wala kwa kitu kingine chochote. Semeni tu "Ndiyo" au "Hapana," na mmaanishe hivyo. Hapo hamtahukumiwa.

decisions.choice: do not swear: Jesus' teaching on oaths
decisions.reason: The verse closely follows Jesus' words in Matthew 5:33-37: do not swear at all, by heaven or by earth, but let your word be yes or no.

decisions.choice: by heaven or by earth: oaths that avoided God's name
decisions.reason: People swore by heaven, earth, Jerusalem or the temple to make a promise binding without naming God (Matthew 5:34-35; 23:16-22). James rules out using oaths to guarantee one's word in everyday speech: a truthful person needs no guarantee.

decisions.choice: let your yes be yes: a plain yes that is true
alternatives: say "yes, yes" as a form of oath
decisions.reason: The article marks the word said: "let your 'Yes' be yes". The second yes says what it must be: a real yes, kept, with nothing added to prop it up.

decisions.choice: fall under judgment (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "fall into hypocrisy" (ὑπόκρισις), which comes from reading ὑπὸ κρίσιν as one word with a preposition before it. The earlier manuscripts and the SBLGNT have "under judgment". This is described from general knowledge and must be checked against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James is writing to the whole community of believers (1:1), women as well as men (2:15 speaks of a brother or sister), so the inclusive default says so. Traditional is one tap away.

decisions.choice: Just say "Yes" or "No" and mean it.
alternatives: Let your yes be yes and your no be no.
decisions.reason: Readable says in plain words what a yes that is yes means (m3).

source.text: Κακοπαθεῖ τις ἐν ὑμῖν; προσευχέσθω· εὐθυμεῖ τις; ψαλλέτω.

records.literal_gloss: Suffers hardship anyone among you? Let him pray; is cheerful anyone? Let him sing praise.

en.L: Is anyone among you suffering hardship? Let {{gender:that person|him}} pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let {{gender:that person|him}} sing praise.
en.B: Is any one of you going through hardship? {{gender:That person|He}} should pray. Is anyone in good spirits? {{gender:That person|He}} should sing praises.
en.R: Are you having a hard time? Then pray. Are you happy? Then sing songs of praise.

es.L: ¿Sufre alguno entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} penalidades? Que ore. ¿Está alguno alegre? Que cante alabanzas.
es.B: ¿Hay alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que esté pasando penalidades? Que ore. ¿Hay alguno que esté de buen ánimo? Que cante alabanzas.
es.R: ¿Lo estás pasando mal? Entonces ora. ¿Estás contento? Entonces canta alabanzas a Dios.

sw.L: Je, yuko mtu kati yenu anayepata taabu? Aombe. Je, yuko aliye mchangamfu? Aimbe sifa.
sw.B: Je, kuna yeyote miongoni mwenu anayepitia taabu? Na aombe. Je, kuna aliye na moyo mchangamfu? Na aimbe nyimbo za sifa.
sw.R: Je, una wakati mgumu? Basi omba. Je, una furaha? Basi imba nyimbo za kumsifu Mungu.

decisions.choice: one record for the whole verse
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates the verse as two questions, each answered by a command, with a raised dot between the first answer and the second question. Dividing by sentences would end a record in the middle of the pairs ("Let him pray; is anyone cheerful?"). The verse is one saying in two matched halves, so it is kept as one record.

decisions.choice: question, then command: if anyone is suffering, let that person pray
decisions.reason: A short question followed by a command works like a condition: whenever this is true, do that. Verse 14 continues the pattern.

decisions.choice: suffering hardship: trouble of any kind
decisions.reason: κακοπαθέω is to endure hardship or ill treatment, the same root as the prophets' suffering in verse 10. It is wider than illness, which verse 14 takes up separately.

decisions.choice: sing praise: praise God in song
decisions.reason: ψάλλω once meant to play a stringed instrument; in the New Testament it is singing praise to God (Romans 15:9; 1 Corinthians 14:15; Ephesians 5:19).

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|him}} and similar spans for the person James describes
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks of "anyone" (τις), a man or a woman, and refers back to that person with a masculine pronoun as Greek does for anyone. The inclusive default names "that person"; the traditional "him" is one tap away.

decisions.choice: Are you having a hard time? Then pray.
alternatives: Is anyone among you suffering? Let that person pray.
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the reader directly, which keeps the condition (m2) and is plainer than "let that person".

decisions.choice: que ore; que cante, no setting
decisions.reason: The Spanish verb says "let that person pray" without a pronoun, so it has no gender and needs no setting here. Where Spanish must use a pronoun or noun for the sick person (verses 14-15, 19-20), it has the same gender setting as the English.

decisions.choice: tú: ¿Lo estás pasando mal? Entonces ora.
alternatives: ¿Alguno de ustedes lo está pasando mal?
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to each reader directly, as the English Readable does. Spanish uses the singular "tú", which addresses any one reader, so these questions have no ustedes/vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: aombe; aimbe, no setting
decisions.reason: Swahili marks "that person" in the verb, which has no gender, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Swahili in verses 13-20.

source.text: ἀσθενεῖ τις ἐν ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Is sick anyone among you?

en.L: Is anyone among you sick?
en.B: Is anyone among you ill?
en.R: Is anyone among you sick?

es.L: ¿Está alguno enfermo entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.B: ¿Hay entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} alguien enfermo?
es.R: ¿Alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} está enfermo?

sw.L: Je, yuko mtu kati yenu aliye mgonjwa?
sw.B: Je, kuna yeyote miongoni mwenu aliye mgonjwa?
sw.R: Je, kuna mtu kati yenu anayeumwa?

decisions.choice: sick: physically ill
decisions.reason: ἀσθενέω means to be weak. Here it is bodily illness, as the anointing, "the one who is sick" (κάμνω, verse 15) and "the Lord will raise him up" show.

decisions.choice: a question that works as a condition, as in verse 13
decisions.reason: "Is anyone sick?" followed by "let him call" means: whoever is sick should call.

source.text: προσκαλεσάσθω τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας, καὶ προσευξάσθωσαν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἀλείψαντες αὐτὸν ἐλαίῳ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου·

records.literal_gloss: Let him call to [himself] the elders of the church, and let them pray over him having anointed him with oil in the name of the Lord;

en.L: Let {{gender:that person|him}} call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over {{gender:that person|him}}, having anointed {{gender:that person|him}} with oil in the name of the Lord.
en.B: {{gender:That person|He}} should call for the elders of the church, and they should pray over {{gender:the sick person|him}} and anoint {{gender:the sick person|him}} with oil in the name of the Lord.
en.R: That person should ask the church leaders to come. The leaders should pray for {{gender:the sick person|him}} and put olive oil on {{gender:them|him}} in the name of the Lord.

es.L: Que llame a los ancianos de la iglesia, y que oren sobre {{gender:esa persona|él}}, habiéndo{{gender:la|lo}} ungido con aceite en el nombre del Señor.
es.B: Que llame a los ancianos de la iglesia, y que ellos oren por {{gender:la persona enferma|el enfermo}} y {{gender:la|lo}} unjan con aceite en el nombre del Señor.
es.R: Que pida a los líderes de la iglesia que vengan. Los líderes deben orar por la persona enferma y ponerle aceite de oliva en el nombre del Señor.

sw.L: Awaite wazee wa kanisa, nao waombe juu yake, wakiwa wamempaka mafuta katika jina la Bwana.
sw.B: Awaite wazee wa kanisa, nao wamwombee na kumpaka mafuta katika jina la Bwana.
sw.R: Mtu huyo awaombe viongozi wa kanisa waje. Viongozi hao wamwombee mgonjwa na kumpaka mafuta ya zeituni katika jina la Bwana.

decisions.choice: the elders of the church: the recognized leaders of the local congregation
decisions.reason: Elders led the early congregations (Acts 14:23; 20:17; 1 Peter 5:1). ἐκκλησία here is the local assembly of believers; in 2:2 James calls their meeting a synagogue.

decisions.choice: anointing with oil: a remedy and a sign of being placed in God's care
decisions.reason: Olive oil was used on wounds and in illness (Isaiah 1:6; Luke 10:34), and the disciples anointed many sick people with oil and healed them (Mark 6:13). Because it is done in the name of the Lord, healing is looked for from the Lord, not from the oil.

decisions.choice: pray over him, having anointed him: the prayer is the main act
decisions.reason: ἀλείψαντες is a participle beside the main verb προσευξάσθωσαν, "let them pray". The anointing comes before or with the prayer, and verse 15 credits the healing to "the prayer of faith".

decisions.choice: in the name of the Lord: calling on the Lord Jesus and acting by his authority
decisions.reason: So the apostles healed "in the name of Jesus Christ" (Acts 3:6; 4:30).

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|him}} and similar spans for the person James describes
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks of "anyone" (τις), a man or a woman, and refers back to that person with a masculine pronoun as Greek does for anyone. The inclusive default names "that person"; the traditional "him" is one tap away.

decisions.choice: church leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" because "elders" can suggest only older people (m1).

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona|él}}; {{gender:la persona enferma|el enfermo}}; {{gender:la|lo}}
decisions.reason: Spanish needs a pronoun or noun here, and the traditional ones ("él", "el enfermo", "lo") are masculine for anyone, as the Greek is. The inclusive default says "esa persona" or "la persona enferma", and the object pronoun agrees with it. Readable says "la persona enferma" and "ponerle", which already include everyone, so it has no span.

source.text: καὶ ἡ εὐχὴ τῆς πίστεως σώσει τὸν κάμνοντα, καὶ ἐγερεῖ αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος· κἂν ἁμαρτίας ᾖ πεποιηκώς, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And the prayer of the faith will save the [one] being sick, and will raise up him the Lord; and if sins he is having committed, it will be forgiven him.

en.L: And the prayer of faith will save the one who is sick, and the Lord will raise {{gender:that person|him}} up; and if {{gender:that person|he}} has committed sins, it will be forgiven {{gender:that person|him}}.
en.B: The prayer made in faith will save the one who is ill, and the Lord will raise {{gender:them|him}} up. And if {{gender:they have|he has}} committed sins, {{gender:they|he}} will be forgiven.
en.R: A prayer made with faith will save the sick person. The Lord will help {{gender:them|him}} get up again. And if {{gender:they have|he has}} sinned, {{gender:they|he}} will be forgiven.

es.L: Y la oración de la fe salvará a {{gender:la persona que está enferma|el que está enfermo}}, y el Señor {{gender:la|lo}} levantará; y si ha cometido pecados, le será perdonado.
es.B: La oración hecha con fe salvará a {{gender:la persona enferma|el enfermo}}, y el Señor {{gender:la|lo}} levantará. Y si ha cometido pecados, le serán perdonados.
es.R: Una oración hecha con fe salvará a {{gender:la persona enferma|el enfermo}}. El Señor {{gender:la|lo}} ayudará a levantarse. Y si ha pecado, será {{gender:perdonada|perdonado}}.

sw.L: Na maombi ya imani yatamwokoa yeye aliye mgonjwa, na Bwana atamwinua; na kama amefanya dhambi, atasamehewa.
sw.B: Maombi yaliyofanywa kwa imani yatamwokoa mgonjwa, na Bwana atamwinua. Na kama ametenda dhambi, atasamehewa.
sw.R: Maombi yanayofanywa kwa imani yatamwokoa mgonjwa. Bwana atamsaidia ainuke tena. Na kama ametenda dhambi, atasamehewa.

decisions.choice: the prayer of faith: prayer that trusts God
decisions.reason: This is the prayer that asks without doubting (1:5-8). Faith here is trust in God to act, and it is the prayer, not the oil, that God answers.

decisions.choice: save: rescue the sick person, with forgiveness in view as well
decisions.reason: σῴζω often means to make well (Mark 5:34; 6:56; 10:52), and "raise up" points first to recovery. Elsewhere in James it means rescue from judgment (1:21; 2:14; 4:12; 5:20), and the forgiveness in the same sentence keeps that wider sense in view. "Save" holds both.

decisions.choice: raise up: from the sickbed
decisions.reason: ἐγείρω is used of getting a sick person up again (Mark 1:31), not here of the resurrection.

decisions.choice: if he has committed sins: not every illness comes from sin, but where it does, it is forgiven
decisions.reason: κἂν, "and if", does not assume the illness was caused by sin (John 9:2-3). Where sin is involved, it is forgiven along with the healing, as in Mark 2:5-11.

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|him}} and similar spans for the person James describes
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks of "anyone" (τις), a man or a woman, and refers back to that person with a masculine pronoun as Greek does for anyone. The inclusive default names "that person"; the traditional "him" is one tap away.

decisions.choice: help them get up again
decisions.reason: Readable says what "raise up" means here (m3).

source.text: ἐξομολογεῖσθε οὖν ἀλλήλοις τὰς ἁμαρτίας καὶ εὔχεσθε ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων, ὅπως ἰαθῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: Confess therefore to one another the sins and pray on behalf of one another, so that you may be healed.

en.L: So confess to one another your sins, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed.
en.B: So make it your practice to confess your sins to each other and to pray for each other, so that you may be healed.
en.R: So tell each other the wrong things you have done, and pray for each other. Then you will be healed.

es.L: {{plural_you:Confiésense|Confesaos}}, pues, unos a otros los pecados, y {{plural_you:oren|orad}} unos por otros, para que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} sanados.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} la costumbre de confesar{{plural_you:se|os}} los pecados unos a otros y de orar unos por otros, para que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} sanados.
es.R: Por eso, {{plural_you:cuéntense|contaos}} unos a otros el mal que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} hecho, y {{plural_you:oren|orad}} unos por otros. Así {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} sanados.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo ungamianeni dhambi, na ombeaneni, ili mponywe.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo jengeni desturi ya kuungamiana dhambi na kuombeana, ili mponywe.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo ambianeni mabaya mliyotenda, na ombeaneni. Ndipo mtaponywa.

decisions.choice: so then: because sin and sickness can belong together
decisions.reason: οὖν draws on verse 15: since forgiveness comes with healing, believers should bring their sins into the open with one another.

decisions.choice: confess to one another, pray for one another: a mutual practice of the whole community
decisions.reason: The confession is to "one another", not only to the elders, and the present tense of ἐξομολογεῖσθε and εὔχεσθε describes an ongoing habit.

decisions.choice: healed: in body, with the healing of the whole person in view
decisions.reason: ἰάομαι continues the healing of the sick in verses 14-15. The same verb is used of healing from sin (1 Peter 2:24; Hebrews 12:13), and here confession and prayer serve both.

decisions.choice: οὖν "so" and ἁμαρτίας "sins" (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts leave out "so", and many later manuscripts read παράπτωμα, "trespasses", for "sins". The meaning does not change. This is described from general knowledge and must be checked against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: make it your practice
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the ongoing sense of the present imperatives (m2).

source.text: πολὺ ἰσχύει δέησις δικαίου ἐνεργουμένη.

records.literal_gloss: Much is strong [the] prayer of [a] righteous [person] working.

en.L: A righteous person's prayer, as it works, is very strong.
en.B: When a righteous person prays, that prayer is at work, and it can do a great deal.
en.R: When someone who does what is right prays, that prayer is strong. It can do a great deal.

es.L: Mucho puede la oración de un justo, mientras actúa.
es.B: Cuando un justo ora, esa oración está en acción, y puede lograr mucho.
es.R: Cuando ora una persona que hace lo correcto, esa oración tiene fuerza. Puede lograr mucho.

sw.L: Dua ya mwenye haki ina nguvu nyingi inapofanya kazi.
sw.B: Mtu mwenye haki anapoomba, ombi lake linafanya kazi, nalo linaweza kutimiza mambo mengi.
sw.R: Mtu anayetenda haki anapoomba, maombi yake yana nguvu. Yanaweza kufanya mambo makubwa.

decisions.choice: as it works: prayer at work in its own action
alternatives: when it is made effective by God
decisions.reason: ἐνεργουμένη is most naturally middle, "working, being active": the prayer of a righteous person has great strength as it does its work. It can also be read as passive, "when it is made effective" (by God), or as describing the prayer as earnest.

decisions.choice: a righteous person: someone who lives rightly before God
decisions.reason: This is not a special class of saints: the next verse makes Elijah "a human being like us". The Lord hears the prayer of the righteous (Proverbs 15:29; Psalm 34:16).

decisions.choice: much it can do: the emphasis falls on "much"
decisions.reason: πολὺ "much" stands first in the sentence for emphasis, before the verb ἰσχύει, "is strong, prevails".

decisions.choice: When a righteous person prays, that prayer ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start from the person praying and end with what the prayer can do, which keeps the emphasis on "much" (m3) at the end of the English sentence.

decisions.choice: Dua ... ina nguvu nyingi
decisions.reason: Swahili cannot put "much" first as the Greek does (m3) without an awkward sentence, so Literal ends on "nguvu nyingi" (much strength), where the stress falls in Swahili.

source.text: Ἠλίας ἄνθρωπος ἦν ὁμοιοπαθὴς ἡμῖν, καὶ προσευχῇ προσηύξατο τοῦ μὴ βρέξαι, καὶ οὐκ ἔβρεξεν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐνιαυτοὺς τρεῖς καὶ μῆνας ἕξ·

records.literal_gloss: Elijah a man was of like nature to us, and with prayer he prayed [for it] not to rain, and not it rained upon the earth years three and months six;

en.L: Elijah was a human being with a nature like ours, and with prayer he prayed that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land [for] three years and six months.
en.B: Elijah was a human being just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and no rain fell on the land for three years and six months.
en.R: Elijah was a person just like us. He prayed hard that it would not rain. And no rain fell on the land for three and a half years.

es.L: Elías era un ser humano de igual naturaleza que nosotros, y con oración oró para que no lloviera, y no llovió sobre la tierra [durante] tres años y seis meses.
es.B: Elías era un ser humano como nosotros. Oró con fervor para que no lloviera, y no cayó lluvia sobre la tierra durante tres años y seis meses.
es.R: Elías era una persona como nosotros. Oró con mucha insistencia para que no lloviera, y no llovió sobre aquella tierra durante tres años y medio.

sw.L: Eliya alikuwa mwanadamu mwenye hali kama yetu, naye aliomba kwa maombi kwamba mvua isinyeshe, na mvua haikunyesha juu ya nchi [kwa] miaka mitatu na miezi sita.
sw.B: Eliya alikuwa mwanadamu kama sisi. Aliomba kwa bidii mvua isinyeshe, na mvua haikunyesha katika nchi kwa miaka mitatu na miezi sita.
sw.R: Eliya alikuwa mtu kama sisi. Aliomba kwa moyo wote mvua isinyeshe. Na mvua haikunyesha katika nchi ile kwa miaka mitatu na nusu.

decisions.choice: with a nature like ours: subject to the same weakness and feelings
decisions.reason: ὁμοιοπαθής means having the same nature and the same experiences. Paul and Barnabas say it of themselves (Acts 14:15). Elijah's prayer was not powerful because he was more than human.

decisions.choice: with prayer he prayed: he prayed earnestly
decisions.reason: Putting a verb with its own noun is a Hebrew way of giving it force (compare Luke 22:15, literally "with desire I have desired").

decisions.choice: the drought: 1 Kings 17-18
decisions.reason: Elijah announced the drought to Ahab (1 Kings 17:1), and the rain returned "in the third year" (1 Kings 18:1). James, like Jesus in Luke 4:25, gives the length as three years and six months. 1 Kings does not say that Elijah prayed for the drought; James draws it from his words "before whom I stand" and from his prayer on Carmel (1 Kings 18:42).

decisions.choice: the land: the land of Israel
decisions.reason: γῆ can mean the earth or a land. The drought fell on Ahab's kingdom and its neighbors (1 Kings 18:10).

decisions.choice: prayed earnestly / prayed hard
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the force of the doubled phrase (m2).

decisions.choice: [for] three years
decisions.reason: English needs "for" to express a length of time; Literal brackets it.

source.text: καὶ πάλιν προσηύξατο, καὶ ὁ οὐρανὸς ὑετὸν ἔδωκεν καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐβλάστησεν τὸν καρπὸν αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And again he prayed, and the heaven rain gave and the earth produced the fruit of it.

en.L: And again he prayed, and the heaven gave rain, and the land brought forth its fruit.
en.B: Then he prayed again, and the sky gave rain and the land produced its crops.
en.R: Then he prayed again. Rain fell from the sky, and the land grew crops again.

es.L: Y de nuevo oró, y el cielo dio lluvia, y la tierra produjo su fruto.
es.B: Luego volvió a orar, y el cielo dio lluvia y la tierra produjo su cosecha.
es.R: Después oró otra vez. Cayó lluvia del cielo, y la tierra volvió a dar cosechas.

sw.L: Na tena aliomba, na mbingu zikatoa mvua, na nchi ikatoa matunda yake.
sw.B: Kisha akaomba tena, na anga likatoa mvua, nayo nchi ikazaa mazao yake.
sw.R: Kisha akaomba tena. Mvua ikanyesha kutoka angani, na nchi ikatoa mazao tena.

decisions.choice: again he prayed: Elijah on Mount Carmel
decisions.reason: Elijah bowed to the ground with his face between his knees, and the sky grew black with clouds and heavy rain fell (1 Kings 18:41-45).

decisions.choice: heaven: the sky, from which rain comes
decisions.reason: οὐρανός is both heaven and sky; paired with the earth it echoes Genesis 1:1, and here it is the sky that gives the rain.

decisions.choice: the land produced its fruit: the harvest the farmer waits for
decisions.reason: "Fruit" (καρπός) repeats the word of verse 7: patient waiting and prayer both look to God for the harvest.

decisions.choice: sky; crops
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "heaven" and "fruit"; Balanced and Readable use the words for rain and harvest (m2, m3).

decisions.choice: cielo at every level
decisions.reason: Spanish "cielo" means both heaven and sky, as the Greek word does (m2), so every level keeps it where the English changes "heaven" to "sky".

source.text: Ἀδελφοί μου, ἐάν τις ἐν ὑμῖν πλανηθῇ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἐπιστρέψῃ τις αὐτόν, γινωσκέτω ὅτι ὁ ἐπιστρέψας ἁμαρτωλὸν ἐκ πλάνης ὁδοῦ αὐτοῦ σώσει ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἐκ θανάτου καὶ καλύψει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Brothers of me, if anyone among you is led astray from the truth and turns back someone him, \v 20 let him know that the [one] having turned back a sinner from [the] wandering of way of him will save soul of him from death and will cover a multitude of sins.

en.L: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, if anyone among you strays from the truth and someone turns {{gender:that person|him}} back, \v 20 let {{gender:that one|him}} know that whoever turns a sinner back from the wandering of {{gender:their|his}} way will save {{gender:their|his}} soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
en.B: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, if one of you wanders away from the truth and someone brings {{gender:that person|him}} back, \v 20 let the one who does so know this: whoever brings a sinner back from the wrong path will save that sinner's soul from death and will cover a great number of sins.
en.R: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, someone among you may wander away from the truth, and another person may bring {{gender:them|him}} back. \v 20 If that happens, the one who brought {{gender:them|him}} back should know this: anyone who turns a sinner away from the wrong path will save that person from death and will bring forgiveness for many sins.

es.L: Hermanos míos, si alguno entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se extravía de la verdad y alguien {{gender:hace volver a esa persona|lo hace volver}}, \v 20 sepa que el que hace volver a un pecador del extravío de su camino salvará su alma de la muerte y cubrirá multitud de pecados.
es.B: Hermanos míos, si alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se aparta de la verdad y otro {{gender:hace volver a esa persona|lo hace volver}}, \v 20 sepa el que lo haga que quien hace volver a un pecador de su camino equivocado salvará de la muerte el alma de ese pecador y cubrirá una gran cantidad de pecados.
es.R: Hermanos míos, puede que alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se aleje de la verdad, y que otro {{gender:haga volver a esa persona|lo haga volver}}. \v 20 Si eso sucede, el que {{gender:hizo volver a esa persona|lo hizo volver}} debe saber esto: quien aparta a un pecador del mal camino salvará a esa persona de la muerte y hará que muchos pecados sean perdonados.

sw.L: Ndugu zangu, mtu yeyote kati yenu akipotoka mbali na kweli, na mtu mwingine akamrudisha, \v 20 na ajue kwamba yeye aliyemrudisha mwenye dhambi kutoka katika upotevu wa njia yake ataiokoa nafsi yake kutoka mautini, na atafunika wingi wa dhambi.
sw.B: Ndugu zangu, ikiwa mmoja wenu atapotoka na kuiacha kweli, na mtu mwingine akamrudisha, \v 20 yule aliyefanya hivyo ajue jambo hili: mtu anayemrudisha mwenye dhambi kutoka katika njia yake potovu ataiokoa nafsi ya mwenye dhambi huyo kutoka mautini, na atafunika dhambi nyingi sana.
sw.R: Ndugu zangu, huenda mmoja wenu akapotea na kuiacha kweli, na mtu mwingine akamrudisha. \v 20 Jambo hilo likitokea, yule aliyemrudisha ajue hili: mtu anayemgeuza mwenye dhambi aiache njia yake mbaya atamwokoa mtu huyo kutoka mautini, na ataleta msamaha wa dhambi nyingi.

decisions.choice: wander from the truth: drift away from the truth believed and lived
decisions.reason: πλανάω (go astray, be led astray) and πλάνη (wandering, error) share a root. In James the truth is the word of truth by which God gave new birth (1:18), to be done and not only heard (1:22); wandering from it is a way of life, not only a mistaken idea. James used the same verb in 1:16, "do not be deceived".

decisions.choice: his soul: the soul of the sinner who is brought back
alternatives: the soul of the one who brings the sinner back
decisions.reason: The nearest person is the sinner ("his way", then "his soul"), and the death is where sin leads (1:15). Some take it as the soul of the one who brings the sinner back (compare Ezekiel 3:21; 1 Timothy 4:16). ψυχή is the whole person and life before God, and θάνατος here is death under judgment, not only bodily death.

decisions.choice: cover a multitude of sins: bring about their forgiveness
alternatives: the sins of the one who brings the sinner back
decisions.reason: To cover sin is to forgive it (Psalm 32:1; 85:3). Proverbs 10:12, "love covers all offenses", lies behind the saying, and 1 Peter 4:8 quotes it too. Most naturally they are the sins of the one brought back; some read them as the rescuer's own.

decisions.choice: γινωσκέτω "let him know" and the place of αὐτοῦ "his" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: save a soul from his death
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read γινώσκετε, "you should know". Some place "his" after "death" ("from his death") and some leave it out. The SBLGNT text is followed. This is described from general knowledge and must be checked against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James is writing to the whole community of believers (1:1), women as well as men (2:15 speaks of a brother or sister), so the inclusive default says so. Traditional is one tap away.

decisions.choice: that sinner's soul (Balanced); that person (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the open "their soul"; Balanced and Readable make the sinner explicit (m2). Readable says "that person" for "soul", the whole person (m2).

decisions.choice: If that happens ... will bring forgiveness for many sins
alternatives: let him know ... will cover a multitude of sins
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two verses with "If that happens" and says what covering sins means (m3).

decisions.choice: nafsi
decisions.reason: "Roho" is also the word for the Spirit and for breath, and could suggest a part of the person. "Nafsi" is the self, the whole person and life before God, as the meaning decision explains (m2). Readable says "mtu huyo", that person, as the English does.
